title: Impact of ChatGPT on ESL students’ academic writing skills: a mixed methods intervention study
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether using ChatGPT as a formative feedback tool improves undergraduate ESL students’ academic writing skills. The study responds to the lack of empirical evidence on generative AI for writing feedback and asks both whether ChatGPT changes writing performance and how students perceive its usefulness. The work is positioned within feedback theory, especially feedback as a dialogic process, and treats ChatGPT as a writing support tool that can provide immediate, tailored responses.

The intervention was conducted in a first-year undergraduate science and engineering context in an elite private university in India. Students in the experimental group received a short training session on using ChatGPT for self-assessment and peer assessment, then used it during six hours of instruction on process, comparison, and cause-effect writing. A comparison group followed the same general course without the ChatGPT feedback intervention. Quantitative data came from pre-test, post-test, and delayed post-test writing assessments; qualitative data came from focus group discussions with experimental-group students.

Results showed a strong positive effect of ChatGPT on writing performance. The experimental group significantly outperformed the comparison group on both the post-test and delayed post-test, and gains persisted over time. Students described ChatGPT as helpful for generating ideas, staying on topic, organizing content, and improving grammar, while also noting minor risks such as dependence and reduced creativity. The paper concludes that, with training, ChatGPT can function as a useful formative feedback tool in large writing classes.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI generative AI chatbot based on a large language model that can provide conversational assistance, explanations, and feedback on text and writing tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as a formative feedback tool for self-assessment and peer-assessment in an undergraduate ESL academic writing intervention, where students used it for idea generation, organization, grammar checking, and revision support.

findings.finding_summary: In this mixed-methods quasi-experimental intervention, the experimental group using ChatGPT for self- and peer-feedback improved from pre-test to post-test and delayed post-test on academic writing scores. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed a significant effect across time, F(2,72)=330.704, p=5.146e-37, b72=0.902; Bonferroni comparisons were significant for pre-test vs post-test (d=-3.300), pre-test vs delayed post-test (d=-3.898), and post-test vs delayed post-test (d=-0.598).
findings.measure: Academic writing test scores across pre-test, post-test, and delayed post-test
findings.sample_size: n=37 (EG); n=35 EG included in reported data per methods section, but tables/reporting use n=37

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods quasi-experimental intervention study with quantitative and qualitative components rather than a randomized controlled trial. The design is informative but still subject to selection and classroom-context confounds.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects on writing performance are very large, with b72=0.902 and multiple statistically significant pairwise comparisons. The positive gains persisted at delayed post-test, indicating a strong educational impact on the measured writing outcome.
